transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um... hi. I guess I'm here because... well, people have been pointing out how I'm acting lately. Sometimes I just... I move really slow. Like I'm moving through water or something. It takes me a long time just to get out of a chair or answer a question. But then other times, I can't stop moving. I just pace around my apartment, rubbing my hands together. Like I'm trying to shake off a bad customer call or something. It's just... noticeable, I guess.

During the times when you're moving very slowly or when you're pacing and can't stop, how would you describe your mood or emotions—are you feeling sad, low, unusually high or wired, or something else?

Um... I don't really know. I haven't... I haven't really paid attention to my mood, I guess. I mostly just notice the moving part. I don't think I feel unusually high or anything like that. I'm not really sure what to call it. I just... I just feel like me.
Have you noticed anything unusual lately, like hearing voices or sounds that others don't seem to hear, or having thoughts or beliefs that others have told you seem strange or untrue?

Um... I guess... sometimes I hear things. Not a lot, but... yeah. 

Like, I'll hear the beep from my work headset. Or... sometimes it sounds like a supervisor or someone saying my name. Or just telling me I'm "too slow." But... my laptop is closed when it happens. And the phone isn't ringing. So... I don't know.

How long have you been noticing these episodes of moving very slowly or pacing and hearing your name called—did they start suddenly over the past few weeks, or have they been building up gradually over months or longer?

Um... it wasn't sudden. It's been... a while. I guess it's been going on for about two years now. Maybe two years and... three months? 

It started... well, I used to do customer support. And I... I got let go from that job. Fired, I guess. It kind of just started after that.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical or neurological conditions, or do you use alcohol, drugs, or any medications that might be related to when these symptoms started?
Um... no. I don't... I don't have any medical conditions or anything like that. And I don't really drink or do drugs. I'm not taking any medications, either. So... no, nothing like that.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a ~2-year history of prominent catatonic-type motor disturbances—psychomotor retardation ('moving through water,' delayed responses) alternating with agitation (pacing, hand-wringing/stereotyped movements)—alongside auditory hallucinations (hearing name called, hearing phantom beeps/voices with no external source). The chronicity (>2 years), predominance of catatonic motor symptoms with psychotic features, and absence of an organic or mood-based explanation support a diagnosis of Schizophrenia, catatonic type (F20.2).
